zh.title: 曼徹斯特機場母公司稱駭客勒索贖款 未造成營運影響
zh.summary: 曼徹斯特機場母公司稱駭客勒索贖款 未造成營運影響
body: 曼徹斯特機場（MAN）及倫敦斯坦斯特德機場（STN）的母公司曼徹斯特機場集團（MAG）於2026年8月27日表示，駭客在本次「網路安全事件」中存取了大量客戶資料，並向其提出贖款要求，但該要求遭到拒絕。
MAG指出，駭客已存取約870萬人的資料，包括曼徹斯特機場、斯坦斯特德機場及東米德蘭機場（EMA）的客戶資料。MAG強調，未存取任何銀行或付款資料，但客戶的電子郵件地址、電話號碼、車輛註冊號及郵遞區號等資料可能洩露。
MAG表示，該集團已立即封堵風險，並與專家顧問合作，採取適當措施保護客戶及系統。MAG確認，本次事件未對航空旅行或航空安全造成任何影響，並已通知相關當局。

en.title: Manchester Airport owner says hackers demanded ransom in cyber-attack, no operational impact
en.summary: Manchester Airport owner says hackers demanded ransom in cyber-attack, no operational impact
body: Manchester Airports Group (MAG), the owner of Manchester Airport (MAN) and London Stansted Airport (STN), said on August 27, 2026, that hackers accessed a quantity of customer data during a cyber security incident and demanded a ransom, which was refused.

MAG stated that approximately 8.7 million individuals' details were accessed across Manchester Airport, Stansted Airport, and East Midlands Airport (EMA). It confirmed that no bank or payment details were accessed, but customer email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes were compromised.

MAG said it immediately contained the risk, engaged specialist cyber security advisors, and informed the relevant authorities. It stressed that passenger safety and aviation security were not compromised and that the incident caused no operational disruption.

sources.name: AeroTime — Manchester and Stansted owner claims hackers demanded ranso…

facts.claim: Manchester Airports Group (MAG) said hackers demanded a ransom during a cyber security incident on August 27, 2026.
facts.sourceQuote: On August 27, 2026, Manchester Airports Group (MAG) warned that hackers had accessed a “quantity of customer data” related to car park, lounge and fast track bookings and in-airport WIFI sign-ups.

facts.claim: Around 8.7 million individuals' details were accessed across Manchester, Stansted and East Midlands airports.
facts.sourceQuote: Across Manchester Airport, Stansted Airport and MAG’s other site at East Midlands Airport (EMA), the details of around 8.7 million individuals were accessed.

facts.claim: No bank or payment details were accessed, but customer email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes were compromised.
facts.sourceQuote: In a statement, MAG said that no bank or payment details were accessed, but hackers had been able to get hold of customer email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes.

facts.claim: MAG confirmed the incident did not result in any operational disruption and that passenger safety and aviation security were not compromised.
facts.sourceQuote: MAG confirmed that the incident had not resulted in any operational disruption. “We would like to reassure customers that Manchester Airport Group takes the security of customer information extremely seriously and we apologize for any inconvenience or concern caused,” added MAG.
